text:
anya: quick heads-up — replay harness (tenant-mix A) shows a KV-cache hit drop ~15% during short microbursts; kernel selector flips to the 'fallback' kernel and p50 doubles under our current delaycap=8ms. attaching short logs and repro below.

tariq: ack. do you have the exact replay command + config?

anya: yup pasted: ```./harness/replay --trace=tenants_A_2026-03-01.bin --rate=burst --burst-size=12 --delaycap_ms=8 --seed=42 --pin-model=v1.3-quant``` also ran synth with `--synth-burst=12` and didn't see the same hit drop.

lucy: interesting — synth vs replay mismatch suggests ordering or prefix caching differences. did you check prefix-length distribution?

anya: prefix med=18 tokens for replay, synth used 16 (I adjusted later to match). after forcing identical prefix dist the KV-hit gap reduced but kernel switch still happens when two tenants hit at near-simultaneous times.

bench-bot: replay-run started (id=e9c2). baseline: delaycap=8ms, batchcap=64, kernel-select=auto.

oliver: can you paste the short profiler output around the flip? even a tiny flame or top lines helps.

anya: copied sample from run e9c2 (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-02T14:12:03Z] tenant=alpha req_id=... kv_hit_rate=0.78 latency_p50=12ms p95=46ms kernel=fast-attn
[2026-03-02T14:12:04Z] tenant=beta req_id=... kv_hit_rate=0.63 latency_p50=24ms p95=98ms kernel=fallback-attn
[2026-03-02T14:12:04Z] selector: chose fallback-attn due to est. memory pressure
perf: top hotspots -> fallback_matmul (31%), kv_cache_miss_path (22%), batch_mux_lock (9%)
```

jordan: hmm selector choosing fallback because of estimated memory pressure — could be our estimator reacting to ephemeral queue length inside batcher. do we log queue length / estimated mem at selection time?

anya: not granularly. I added a quick trace that logs batcher.queue_len + estimated_kv_mem before selection and saw spikes to 9 while single tenant burst hit.

tariq: suggestion: run apples-to-apples by pinning these: model+quant, seq_len dist, client inter-arrival RNG seed, and stricter tenant pacing. then compare kernel logs and KV hit traces. we should also try delaycap sweep (2ms/4ms/8ms/12ms) and batchcap sweep (16/32/64) to map where the flip is.

lucy: agreed. also run with kernel-logging on (env KERNEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug) for 1 minute window around expected flip. we need to verify if selector threshold is too sensitive to transient queue jitter.

oliver: adding a short repro command for deterministic run: ```./harness/replay --trace=tenants_A_2026-03-01.bin --seed=42 --pin-model=v1.3-quant --seq-dist=from-trace --clients=8 --pacing=deterministic --delaycap_ms=8 --batchcap=32 --log-kernel=1 > run_e9c2.log```

anya: ran that; attached the diff between runs with batchcap=32 vs 64: kernel flips at ~t=35s for batchcap=64, but stays on fast-attn for 32. kv-hit better with 32 (0.82 vs 0.67).

jordan: that points to batching heuristics — larger batchcap allows more enqueueing which inflates est. mem and triggers fallback. two options: tighten mem estimator or prefer KV-friendly kernels when KV-hit above X.

tariq: both are viable. quick experiment idea: change selector policy to include a KV-hit bias term: score = base_score - alpha*kv_miss_rate. if score_fallback < score_fast then prefer fast. can simulate offline using traces.

lucy: also consider a small conservative change: reduce max_delay_ms from 8 to 6 for tenant-mix A only, see if latency SLO still ok. that cuts the enqueuing window.

anya: ran a short sweep 4/6/8/12 with batchcap=64: results (p50/p95, kv-hit):
- 4ms: 11ms / 40ms, kv=0.83
- 6ms: 12ms / 46ms, kv=0.78
- 8ms: 18ms / 90ms, kv=0.65 (flips at ~35s)
- 12ms: 19ms / 110ms, kv=0.63

oliver: solid data. looks like there's a threshold between 6 and 8 where batching causes the selector to mis-evaluate. can we repro with synthetic arrivals that exactly mimic trace interleaving? that will help isolate ordering vs content.

anya: noted — I can dump the exact interleaving stream and feed to synth harness.

jordan: for apples-to-apples comparsion include: (1) identical request ordering, (2) pinned model+quant, (3) identical client clocks, (4) same runtime flags (delaycap/batchcap). We'll run a matrix and then run selector-sim offline to see if scoring function flips.

tariq: one more operational thought — add a temporary logging gate so when kernel changes we emit full batch metadata: tenant list, kv_hits, queue_len, estimated_mem. that'll make postmortem easier. low overhead if gated.

anya: done — pushed a gated log to canary. bench-bot: can we schedule a matrix run: delaycap=[4,6,8] x batchcap=[32,64] x run-type=[replay,synth] with seed=42 ?

bench-bot: scheduled job matrix id=m-431 for 2102469000 start. notifications on #eng-runtime when done. :white_check_mark:

lucy: nice. once results land I'll run offline selector-sim and try alpha tuning for the KV-bias term. aim to have a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

oliver: if we go with selector change, plan a canary with very low traffic first, and a rollback if p95 regresses for any tenant.

anya: thanks all — will post the matrix outputs here. if anyone wants immediate access to logs I pushed to s3://redwood-bench/runs/e9c2/ (read-only for eng).

jordan: good triage. follow-ups: (a) reproduce with synth ordering, (b) collect gated kernel-change dumps, (c) offline selector-sim with kv-bias. assign to tariq+lucy+anya.

anya: assigning now.

tariq: taking it.

lucy: taking sim + tuning.

anya: I'll triage logs and check canary results.

bench-bot: matrix job m-431 completed: summary -> (4ms,32,replay) ok, (4ms,64,replay) ok, (6ms,32,replay) ok, (6ms,64,replay) ok, (8ms,32,replay) ok, (8ms,64,replay) kernel-flip observed at ~36s. full artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/m-431/

lucy: grabbing artifacts now. will run selector-sim and post numbers.

oliver: thanks — let's keep the canary patch small.

anya: thanks team :)
